title: Strategic companies
description: A set of companies is strategic if it makes every good, is closed under control, and no proper subset has both properties; deciding whether a given company is strategic is Sigma-2-complete (Cadoli, Eiter and Gottlob). The abstraction guesses a closed producing set with company b, and the check looks for a smaller one. The check writes the refinement itself as clause/3 atoms, one clause per company it could drop.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The holding: who makes what, who controls whom. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.
group(T,K) :- owner(T,K,_).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): producing, closed sets that contain the query company.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a set of companies ...
{ in(C) } :- company(C).
% ... that makes every good ...
:- good(G), not in(C) : makes(C,G).
% ... is closed under control ...
:- group(T,K), not in(T), in(O) : owner(T,K,O).
% ... and contains the company we ask about.
:- query(C), not in(C).
#show in/1.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the members of the set.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a proper subset with the same two properties (solver C) and states the refinement as clause/3 atoms.
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: a proper subset of the candidate that also makes every good and is
% closed under control. Then the candidate is not minimal.
{ sub(C) } :- in(C).
:- good(G), not sub(C) : makes(C,G).
:- group(T,K), not sub(T), sub(O) : owner(T,K,O).
dropped(C) :- in(C), not sub(C).
smaller :- dropped(C).
:- not smaller.
#show sub/1.

% The subset refutes every set that contains it and one more company. For each dropped
% company D, clause D says: a member of the subset leaves, or D leaves.
% (Leaving out the last literal would also forbid the subset itself, which may be strategic.)
clause(D, in(C), false) :- dropped(D), sub(C).
clause(D, in(D), false) :- dropped(D).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The check writes the refinement itself, as clause(Id, Atom, Value) atoms: one clause
# per company that the smaller set leaves out. G.clauses(X) turns them into clauses.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X: reject M with G.clauses(X)

instances.facts:
% A holding owns the companies a..h, which make the goods 1..6.
company(a;b;c;d;e;f;g;h).
good(1..6).
% makes(C,G): company C makes good G.
makes(a,1). makes(e,1).
makes(b,2). makes(d,2). makes(g,2).
makes(a,3). makes(b,3).
makes(e,4). makes(g,4).
makes(d,5). makes(e,5).
makes(b,6). makes(c,6). makes(f,6).
% owner(T,K,O): O belongs to the K-th group of companies that together control company T.
owner(b,1,a). owner(b,1,c).
owner(e,1,b). owner(e,1,h).
owner(e,2,g). owner(e,2,h).
owner(f,1,h).
owner(f,2,b). owner(f,2,e). owner(f,2,g).
% Is this company strategic, that is, in some strategic set?
query(b).

% Three companies, two goods; a and b each make both, c only the first, and b
% controls a. Every producing, closed set with c has a smaller one without it: c is
% in no strategic set.
company(a;b;c).
good(1;2).
makes(a,1). makes(a,2).
makes(b,1). makes(b,2).
makes(c,1).
owner(a,1,b).                         % b controls a
query(c).

% Four companies, three goods; a and b together control d.
company(a;b;c;d).
good(1..3).
makes(a,1). makes(b,1).
makes(c,2). makes(d,2).
makes(a,3). makes(d,3).
owner(d,1,a). owner(d,1,b).
query(d).
